body:
## Problem

id(web/image-browser): the image browser shape-trusts the `/api/images` response — a wrong-shape 200 response either dumps a raw engine TypeError into the dialog or, worse, silently renders bogus cards that insert a src-less image node into the document.

`pkgs/id/web/src/image-browser.ts`:

- `:245` — `return (await response.json()) as ImageEntry[];` in `fetchImages()` is a bare cast; the result is consumed unvalidated by the `.then` handler in `openImageBrowser`.
- `:146` — the handler wipes the grid first (`grid.textContent = ""`, clearing the "Loading…" state), then reads `images.length` (`:148`) and iterates (`:156`), dereferencing `img.hash` / `img.url` / `img.name` per element with no shape check.
- `:212` — the `.catch` surfaces the raw exception (`Failed to load images: ${err}`), so a shape failure shows e.g. "Failed to load images: TypeError: {} is not iterable" to the user.
- A string payload is iterable, so it never throws: each character becomes a "card" with `name`/`url`/`hash` all undefined, the Insert button enables on selection, and `insertImage` (`:216-224`) creates an image node with `src: undefined, alt: undefined`.

The server contract is a bare JSON array (`pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:2238` `images_list_handler` returns `Json(Vec<ImageEntry>)`), so a wrong-shape 200 requires deploy skew, a proxy/error envelope, or a future contract change — exactly the boundary this cast refuses to check. Sibling of #7811 (home feed, same wipe/cast pattern, different module and endpoint).

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ origin/main fd2b0c84f8, image-browser.ts md5 9f5336c522ed40f25ac493a4a7215f24)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-image-browser/probe.ts` (bun, minimal DOM stub, real module imported from a clean `git archive origin/main` snapshot at `~/git/fleet/probe-main-a`; fetch stubbed per case):

- control (well-formed `[{hash:"abc123", name:"cat.png", url:"/api/images/abc123", size:42}]`): renders 1 card, name `cat.png`, hash `abc123` — OK
- `null` body: grid shows `Failed to load images: TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'images.length')`, 0 cards
- `{}` body: grid shows `Failed to load images: TypeError: {} is not iterable`, 0 cards
- `[null]`: grid shows `Failed to load images: TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'img.hash')`, 0 cards
- `[valid, null]`: throws on the second element; the catch's `grid.textContent =` assignment wipes even the already-appended valid card — 0 cards, raw TypeError
- `"abc"` body: NO error — 3 bogus cards render, every name `undefined`; selecting one enables Insert, and clicking Insert creates an image node with attrs `{}` (`src`/`alt` undefined)

The existing test file (`pkgs/id/web/src/image-browser.test.ts`) mocks only the well-formed array (line 17) — no malformed-shape cases.

## Why it matters

The image browser is how users insert previously uploaded images. Failing closed here is cheap: validate the array shape at the fetch boundary and show the designed failure message. Today a malformed payload either leaks a raw TypeError as the dialog's only content or — in the string case — lets a user insert a broken, src-less image node into a real document with no error anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A malformed `/api/images` payload (null body, non-array body, null or wrong-typed elements/fields) does NOT render any cards and does NOT enable Insert.
- [ ] A malformed payload surfaces the clean failure message (e.g. "Failed to load images.") — never a raw TypeError/engine message.
- [ ] A partially valid array (`[valid, null]`) does not leave a half-rendered grid (all-or-nothing rendering).
- [ ] Well-formed payloads render exactly as today (existing image-browser.test.ts cases unchanged and green).
- [ ] New regression tests in `pkgs/id/web/src/image-browser.test.ts` cover the malformed cases above and fail pre-fix.
- [ ] Web suite + typecheck green.
